basis: Defining glycosylation, neurodevelopmental and visual disorder; anemia 5/7 and antithrombin deficiency 5/5. Dermatitis/ichthyosis 4-5/7 omitted at cap; transaminases alone insufficient for hepatic damage.

decisions.haematologic: involved: anemia in 5/7 and reduced antithrombin activity in 5/5 demonstrate common blood/coagulation dysfunction.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability, developmental impairment and cerebellar abnormalities define the syndrome; intellectual disability in 7/7.
decisions.ocular: primary: severe visual impairment and structural ocular abnormalities define the syndrome; visual loss in 7/7.
decisions.dermatologic: none: dermatitis 5/7 and ichthyosis 4/7 qualify, but omitted under the four-organ cap in favor of severe neurologic, ocular and blood dysfunction.

basis: Skin hypopigmentation, ocular and brain anomalies define the syndrome; defining acral skeletal malformations support musculoskeletal involvement despite unavailable frequencies.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular anomalies are explicitly part of the defining syndrome name; no contradictory definition is supplied.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: acral skeletal malformations and craniofacial asymmetry are defining components; included by the diagnostic-feature exception.

basis: Pituitary infarction/hemorrhage; chiasmal dysfunction causes hemianopia in 80-99%, and cranial nerve paralysis occurs in 30-79%. These localize to neurologic structures.

decisions.ocular: none: typical bitemporal hemianopia arises from optic chiasm compression; ocular motor palsies reflect cranial nerve injury rather than direct eye damage.

basis: Defining hair/skin and cardiac disease; hydrocephalus 30-79%, skeletal maturation delay 80-99% and pectus 30-79%. Group-wide GH deficiency frequency is unclear.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: associated GH deficiency lacks a reliable group-wide frequency or major diagnostic status; short stature alone does not establish endocrine damage.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: delayed skeletal maturation occurs in 80-99% and pectus excavatum in 30-79%, supporting common structural skeletal involvement.

basis: Neurodegeneration, pulmonary fibrosis and cerebral angiomatosis define FINCA; chronic hemolytic anemia 3/3. Malabsorption/diarrhea 3/3 omitted at cap; liver dysfunction transient.

decisions.haematologic: involved: chronic hemolytic anemia in 3/3 demonstrates direct, persistent blood-cell damage.
decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cerebral angiomatosis is a named defining vascular lesion; vessels belong to the cardiovascular axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: malabsorption with diarrhea in 3/3 qualifies, but omitted at the four-organ cap, prioritizing defining cerebropulmonary/vascular disease and chronic hemolysis.

basis: Historical G6PD class V denotes increased enzyme activity without established hemolysis; metabolic classification retained without inferring anemia from synonyms.

decisions.haematologic: none: historical class V variants have increased G6PD activity without established hemolytic disease; erythrocyte enzyme measurement alone is insufficient.

basis: Defining osteolysis, lipodystrophy and skin atrophy (80-99%); characteristic progressive nephropathy, stage 5 CKD annotated 1/1. Dental anomalies 30-79% omitted at cap.

decisions.renal: involved: progressive nephropathy is characteristic of type B disease; stage 5 CKD is annotated in 1/1, although population frequency is imprecise.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental abnormalities occur in 30-79% and qualify, but omitted under the four-organ cap in favor of progressive renal disease.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: thin/atrophic skin and generalized loss of subcutaneous fat are defining progeroid features; thin skin occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Barmah Forest alphavirus infection; common arthralgia and transient rash do not establish lasting joint or skin damage in at least 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent arthralgia does not establish damaging arthritis; persistent objective joint damage in at least 30% is not established.

basis: Muscular dystrophy with cerebellar atrophy 5/9 and cataracts 6/18 (~33%). Hearing loss 1/1 does not establish prevalence; respiratory impairment reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.otologic: none: hearing loss in one assessed patient does not establish occurrence in at least 30% of the broader disease cohort or a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Congenital esophageal discontinuity; associated tracheoesophageal fistula directly creates an abnormal airway connection in approximately 85-90%.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: tracheoesophageal fistula occurs in approximately 85-90% and directly affects tracheal anatomy; it is part of the usual congenital malformation complex.
